models.sample_description: Firm-year 10-K observations with filings of at least 3,000 words from 1994–2014, matched to weekly CRSP returns and Compustat data. review_notes: Table 3 is the principal full-sample family: Equation (4) tests modified Fog readability against one-year-ahead crash risk using NCSKEW, DUVOL, and CRASH as parallel outcomes. The Introduction separately highlights the earnings-management interaction and later tables test cross-sectional partitions; those are other contributions/secondary tests rather than additional baseline outcomes for the selected readability-to-crash-risk question.

The Table 3 baseline contains all 16 RHS terms in Equation (4), including OPAQUE squared, and includes year and industry fixed effects, an unreported intercept, and standard errors clustered by firm. The three columns each report N=52,879.

Supporting fitted inputs include the expanded index model that generates W, the modified-Jones fit that generates ABACC for OPAQUE, and the CAPM beta fit used for BETA. The paper does not report the modified-Jones equation or CAPM equation/estimator; the expanded index model estimator is also unspecified. These remain explicit gaps.

The source gives conflicting MODFOG word-list thresholds: the measurement section says at least three syllables, whereas the Table 3 note and Appendix say the words exceed three syllables. The exact threshold is unresolved. The HHI share formula and the industry classification used for fixed effects are also not stated.
results_review_notes: Table 1 Panel A has the same 52,879-observation full sample as Table 3; each row retains N, mean, standard deviation, Q1, median, and Q3 as printed. RAWFOG is linked only as the upstream raw version of MODFOG. The reported OPAQUE row is exact for OPAQUE and a component of the retained squared term; no squared-term statistics were calculated.
Table 1 Panel B reports one-year-ahead outcome means by MODFOG tercile. Tercile N is not reported. The high-versus-low p-values are univariate tests and were not recorded as data-value descriptives.
The Table 3 notes explicitly identify the intercept as unreported; all 16 frozen predictors are tabulated in each selected outcome column. Year and industry fixed effects are reported as Yes.

The original Table 3 p. 47 PDF is the authority for superscript star counts; several markers were omitted or garbled in the verified text. The current extraction preserves the viewed table markers and p. 48 legend.

Table 1 Panel B reports univariate means of crash outcomes by MODFOG tercile but omits tercile sample Ns; the retained groups preserve this limitation and do not copy Panel B p-values as data descriptives.
The Table 3 p. 47 note says the 2,028 words exceed three syllables, while the method section pp. 14–15 says at least three syllables; the frozen specification’s threshold ambiguity is preserved.
